text: dsh-kimi-computer-use 是一款面向 macOS 的 DSH 插件，将 Kimi Computer Use 的 stdio MCP 服务接入 DSH，并自动注册随包提供的操作技能。它通过通用 MCP 客户端发现 KimiCU 工具，也将技能目录挂载到 DSH。用户可借此查看应用状态、点击和输入、滚动或拖动，并在每次操作后重新读取界面状态。适合希望让 DSH 助手操作 Mac 图形应用的用户；需要 Apple Silicon Mac、运行中的 KimiCU.app 及 DSH。

dsh-kimi-computer-use connects Kimi Computer Use to DSH through a stdio MCP client and registers its bundled skill. Users can inspect app state, click, type, scroll, or drag, then reread the interface. It helps DSH users operate Mac apps; it requires Apple Silicon, KimiCU.app, and DSH.
想让 DSH 助手帮我查看 Mac 上当前打开了哪些应用。
能不能让 DSH 操作 macOS 图形界面里的应用？
我想让助手点击窗口、填写表单并确认操作结果。
让 DSH 能读取应用界面状态，再按界面元素执行操作。
需要一个能通过自然语言操作 Mac 桌面应用的 DSH 扩展。
如何让 DSH 助手在应用里输入文字、滚动和拖动？
I want my DSH assistant to inspect and operate Mac apps.
Let DSH click, type, and read the current state of a macOS app.
dsh-kimi-computer-use 的功能「tools」：DSH 可通过 stdio MCP 启动 KimiCU，并发现其提供的应用操作工具；工具以 mcp__cu__ 前缀呈现。
dsh-kimi-computer-use 的功能「skill」：插件会把自身随包的 kimi-computer-use 技能目录注册到 DSH，无需手动复制技能文件。
dsh-kimi-computer-use 的功能「inspect」：用户可先列出打开的应用，再读取目标应用的当前界面状态，以确定可操作元素。
dsh-kimi-computer-use 的功能「interact」：技能支持点击、输入、按键、滚动、设置字段值、选择文本、拖动及次级操作，并建议每次动作后重新读取状态。
dsh-kimi-computer-use 的功能「refresh」：界面变化后应重新读取状态并取得新元素索引或坐标，避免继续使用已失效的位置。
dsh-kimi-computer-use 需要 Apple Silicon Mac、macOS 14 或更高版本，以及已安装并保持运行且获辅助功能和屏幕录制授权的 KimiCU.app。

dsh-kimi-computer-use README · dsh-kimi-computer-use：[中文](README.zh.md)

A [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) bundle that wires [Kimi Computer Use](https://www.kimi.com/)'s stdio MCP server into DSH through the generic [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client) bridge, plus a bundled skill that drives it once connected.

dsh-kimi-computer-use README · dsh-kimi-computer-use：This is a third-party interoperability plugin. Its inclusion does not imply endorsement, recommendation, partnership, or ongoing support by DeepSeek or by Moonshot AI (the maker of Kimi Computer Use).

dsh-kimi-computer-use README · What this bundle does and does not do：| Concern | This bundle | You / KimiCU.app |
|---|---|---|
| Insert one `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` row that starts `kimi-cu mcp` over stdio | Yes | — |
| Discover and register KimiCU's MCP tools as `mcp__cu__<tool>` | Yes | — |
| Register the bundled `kimi-computer-use` skill (interaction loop + safety rules) | Yes | — |
| Download, verify, or install `KimiCU.app` | No | Yes — install from the official Kimi channel |
| Bundle ID / arm64 / Team ID / `codesign` verification | No | Handled by KimiCU.app's own installer |
| Start, stop, or supervise the KimiCU background service | No | Yes — keep the app running yourself |
| Grant Accessibility / Screen Recording permissions | No | Yes — grant them in the KimiCU.app UI |

text:
dsh-kimi-computer-use README · Requirements：- Apple Silicon Mac, macOS 14 or later.
- [`KimiCU.app`](https://www.kimi.com/) installed from the official Kimi channel and left running, with Accessibility and Screen Recording granted in its own UI.
- A DSH installation (`@deepseek-ai/dsh`) whose `dsh` CLI ships `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` in-box (true for published `@deepseek-ai/dsh >= 0.1.1-rc.2`).

dsh-kimi-computer-use README · Install：Into a profile (see the [plugin-and-profile tutorial](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/main/docs/user/develop/basic/publish.md) for the full mechanism):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile demo add dsh-kimi-computer-use          # once published to npm
dsh plugin --profile demo add ./dsh-kimi-computer-use        # from a local checkout
dsh plugin --profile demo add github:<you>/dsh-kimi-computer-use#<sha>   # from git, pinned to a commit
```

dsh-kimi-computer-use README · Install：The git form runs this package's `prepare` script to build `lib/skills.js` from source; pnpm ≥10 blocks that script until you allow it. If `dsh plugin` reports the build was blocked, add the exact package key it printed to the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`:

```yaml
allowBuilds:
  dsh-kimi-computer-use: true
```

then re-run the `add` command. Only allow builds for a package whose source you trust, and pin a commit so a later push cannot silently change what runs at install time.

dsh-kimi-computer-use README · Install：Verify without booting, then boot:

```sh
dsh --profile demo --dump-config   # shows a "# == dsh-kimi-computer-use" layer
dsh --profile demo
```

Remove with `dsh plugin --profile demo remove dsh-kimi-computer-use`.

dsh-kimi-computer-use README · Verify：1. After boot, wait for the `mcp__cu__*` tools to appear (discovery is asynchronous).
2. Ask the agent to list open applications. Confirm it calls `mcp__cu__list_apps` (or the equivalent discovered tool) and returns a real result from your running KimiCU.app.
3. For any GUI action, the bundled skill instructs the agent to state what will happen and get your confirmation before anything hard to reverse (sending, deleting, purchasing, publishing).

dsh-kimi-computer-use README · Security：KimiCU.app's own installer verifies its Bundle ID, arm64 architecture, and Apple `codesign` signature before installing itself; none of that runs through this bundle. Only install `KimiCU.app` from the official Kimi channel. Only allow a git-hosted install's build script for a source you trust, pinned to a specific commit.

dsh-kimi-computer-use README · Development：```sh
npm install
npm run check   # build then test
npm pack --dry-run
```

dsh-kimi-computer-use README · Releases：Every new commit pushed to `main` is validated and automatically released to npm, tagged as `vX.Y.Z`, and published as a GitHub Release with generated release notes. If the version in `package.json` is already published, the workflow increments the patch version automatically.

Publishing uses npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC), not a long-lived npm token. Before the first release, configure an npm Trusted Publisher for package `dsh-kimi-computer-use` with:

dsh-kimi-computer-use README · Releases：- Organization or user: `dshapp`
- Repository: `dsh-kimi-computer-use`
- Workflow filename: `release.yml`
- Environment: `npm`

The repository's GitHub Actions workflow permissions must also allow read and write access so it can push the version commit and tag and create the GitHub Release.
